question: Is the visitor record I got when I extended my stay the same thing as a Canadian visitor visa?
generated_answer:
No, the visitor record is not the same as a Canadian visitor visa. A visitor record is a document that shows the date by which you must leave Canada. It is issued to visitors who extend their stay in Canada. A Canadian visitor visa, on the other hand, is a document that allows you to enter Canada as a visitor. If you need to extend your stay in Canada, you will need to apply for a visitor record, not a new visitor visa.

If you have a visitor record and you want to leave Canada and then re-enter, you will need to meet the entry requirements for visitors, which may include having a valid visitor visa if you are from a country that requires one.

It's important to understand the difference between these two documents to ensure that you comply with Canadian immigration rules. If you have any doubts or questions, it's best to consult with Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) or seek advice from an immigration professional.
